chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jareer, from Abu Al-Rabie, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who married a woman, so he stayed with her for days, not being able to consummate the marriage, except that he had seen from her what is prohibited to others. Then he divorced her. Is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: Is it permissible for him, given that he had seen from her mother what he had seen?

key_terms.يَحْرُمُ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ: Prohibited to others (referring to private parts)

ai.seo_question: Does a man who sees his wife's private parts but does not consummate the marriage become prohibited from marrying her daughter?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling of *ikhtilal* (marriageability) by establishing that merely seeing a wife's private parts (*nazar*) creates a prohibitive bond equivalent to consummation, thereby preventing the man from marrying her daughter. This view is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it expands the definition of 'seeing' beyond mere visual contact to include the specific act of viewing the *awrah*, distinguishing it from the majority opinion which often requires actual sexual intercourse for such prohibitions to apply. The hadith underscores the principle that the barrier to marriage is rooted in the intimacy established through the marital contract and the specific act of unveiling, rather than solely on physical union.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who married a woman, so he stayed for days with her, not going to bed with her, apart from that he had seen from her what is Prohibited unto others. Then he divorced her. Is it correct for him that he marries her daughter?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How can it be correct for him and he had seen from her mother what he had seen?’
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi‘ who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who marries a woman and lives with her for many days, unable to do anything except that he has seen from her what is unlawful for others to see; then he divorces her; if he can marry her daughter. He (the Imam) said, ’How can it be proper for him when he has seen of her mother what he has seen?’”
